tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

## zotero-research
Read-only access to the user's Zotero research library. For substantive sport-science questions, build a Zotero-first evidence pack before answering. Return bounded page-located evidence, label external fallback sources explicitly, and never represent a Reference Stub as a reviewed Paper Brief. SecondBrain Queue is the priority lane; promotion eligibility is controlled by promotion_scope.

---
name: typesafe-ai
license: MIT
description: >
  Build AI-powered software with TypeSafe: small units of AI intelligence you
  can use like programming primitives. Its System One models, including Jev,
  turn natural language and application state into typed judgments and
  probabilities that code can combine. Use when a feature needs programmable
  common sense, when brainstorming what AI could make possible in an app, or
  when an LLM prompt-and-parse step could become a structured decision.
  Applications include routing, ranking, extraction, verification, and
  interactive experiences; these are starting points, not the limits.
  Read live docs and cookbooks to find useful patterns and discover new combinations.
---

# Build with TypeSafe

TypeSafe makes units of AI intelligence usable like programming primitives: small
judgments you can compose into larger capabilities. Its **System One models** return
fast, focused judgments that software can consume directly. **Jev** is TypeSafe's
flagship and first System One model. It understands natural language and returns
typed answers and probabilities rather
than generating text or reasoning explanations. Code owns the workflow; the model
supplies programmable common sense where ordinary code needs semantic understanding.

## Read the live docs

**The live TypeSafe docs are the source of truth. Read them as part of the task.**
This skill gives direction; the docs carry current concepts, prompting guidance,
API contracts, SDK usage, models, limits, and worked examples.

- Start with the [documentation index](https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt) to discover
  relevant pages and cookbooks. Use targeted reads rather than loading the entire site.
- Mintlify serves Markdown by appending `.md` to a page path, for example
  [how to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md).
  Follow links from the index; convert extensionless documentation page links to
  `.md` when useful. Resolve relative links against `https://docs.typesafe.ai`.
- Before writing an integration, read the current API or chosen SDK page and the

set -e
D="$HOME/.claude/jobs/9378b738/tmp/TypeSafe_Sandbox"
cd "$D"

cat > setup_global_key.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the TypeSafe API key once, globally, on macOS.
#
# The key goes into the macOS Keychain (service: typesafe-api-key). A line added to
# ~/.zshenv exports it as TYPESAFE_API_KEY for every zsh, including the
# non-interactive shells Claude Code spawns. That line holds no secret, so it is
# safe even if your dotfiles are in a git repo.
#
# Run this in Terminal.app, NOT through Claude Code. The prompt needs a real
# terminal, and anything typed into a Claude session is written to a transcript
# that is tracked in the dotclaude repo.
#
# Usage:  ./setup_global_key.sh          install or update the key
#         ./setup_global_key.sh --check  report status, change nothing

set -euo pipefail

SERVICE="typesafe-api-key"
ZSHENV="$HOME/.zshenv"
MARKER="# >>> typesafe api key >>>"
END_MARKER="# <<< typesafe api key <<<"

if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]]; then
  echo "This installer is macOS only (it uses the Keychain). See docs/STATUS.md for Windows." >&2
  exit 1
fi

keychain_has_key() {
  security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "$SERVICE" -w >/dev/null 2>&1
}

zshenv_has_block() {
  [[ -f "$ZSHENV" ]] && grep -qF "$MARKER" "$ZSHENV"
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--check" ]]; then
  keychain_has_key && echo "keychain:  key present (service $SERVICE)" || echo "keychain:  MISSING"
  zshenv_has_block && echo "zshenv:    export block present" || echo "zshenv:    MISSING"
  echo "this shell: TYPESAFE_API_KEY is ${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:+set}${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-NOT SET}"
  exit 0
fi

# --- 1. get the key, without it ever reaching a screen, a log, or shell history ---
if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: no terminal on stdin." >&2
  echo "Open Terminal.app and run this script there. Do not run it through Claude Code:" >&2
  echo "the prompt cannot read input, and the key would land in a tracked transcript." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if keychain_has_key; then
  echo "A key is already in the Keychain under service '$SERVICE'."
  printf "Replace it? [y/N] "
  read -r reply
  [[ "$reply" == [yY] ]] || { echo "Left the existing key alone."; exit 0; }
fi

printf "Paste your TypeSafe API key (input is hidden, from https://console.typesafe.ai/): "
IFS= read -rs API_KEY
printf "\n"

if [[ -z "${API_KEY:-}" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: empty input, nothing written." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# -A allows any process running as you to read the item with no GUI prompt. Without
# it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang the shell.
# -U updates the item if it already exists.
security add-generic-password \
  -a "$USER" \
  -s "$SERVICE" \
  -l "TypeSafe API key" \
  -D "application password" \
  -j "Used by TYPESAFE_API_KEY, exported from ~/.zshenv" \
  -w "$API_KEY" \
  -A -U
unset API_KEY
echo "Stored in the Keychain under service '$SERVICE'."

# --- 2. export it from ~/.zshenv, idempotently ---
# .zshenv, not .zshrc: only .zshenv is sourced for non-interactive shells, which is
# what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
if zshenv_has_block; then
  echo "~/.zshenv already has the export block, leaving it as is."
else
  [[ -f "$ZSHENV" ]] && cp "$ZSHENV" "$ZSHENV.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
  cat >> "$ZSHENV" <<'BLOCK'

# >>> typesafe api key >>>
# Reads from the macOS Keychain. Contains no secret, safe to commit.
# The guard means the `security` call runs once per process tree, not per subshell.
if [ -z "${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  export TYPESAFE_API_KEY="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s typesafe-api-key -w 2>/dev/null)"
fi
# <<< typesafe api key <<<
BLOCK
  echo "Added the export block to ~/.zshenv (previous version backed up if it existed)."
fi

# --- 3. verify, without printing the key ---
FETCHED="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "$SERVICE" -w 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "$FETCHED" ]]; then
  echo "Verified: the Keychain returns a value of ${#FETCHED} characters."
else
  echo "WARNING: could not read the key back from the Keychain." >&2
  exit 1
fi
unset FETCHED

cat <<'NEXT'

Done. Two things left, in this order:
  1. Restart Claude Code. A running session keeps the environment it started with,
     so it will not see the new variable until it is restarted.
  2. Run the smoke test:  python smoke_test.py

To re-check status later:  ./setup_global_key.sh --check
NEXT
EOF
chmod +x setup_global_key.sh
bash -n setup_global_key.sh && echo "SYNTAX OK"

cd "$D"

cat > setup_global_key.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the TypeSafe API key once, globally, on macOS.
#
# The key goes into the macOS Keychain (service: typesafe-api-key). A line added to
# ~/.zshenv exports it as TYPESAFE_API_KEY for every zsh, including the
# non-interactive shells Claude Code spawns. That line holds no secret, so it is
# safe even if your dotfiles are in a git repo.
#
# Run this in Terminal.app, NOT through Claude Code. The prompt needs a real
# terminal, and anything typed into a Claude session is written to a transcript
# that is tracked in the dotclaude repo.
#
# Usage:  ./setup_global_key.sh          install or update the key
#         ./setup_global_key.sh --check  report status, change nothing

set -euo pipefail

SERVICE="typesafe-api-key"
ZSHENV="$HOME/.zshenv"
MARKER="# >>> typesafe api key >>>"
END_MARKER="# <<< typesafe api key <<<"

if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]]; then
  echo "This installer is macOS only (it uses the Keychain). See docs/STATUS.md for Windows." >&2
  exit 1
fi

keychain_has_key() {
  security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "$SERVICE" -w >/dev/null 2>&1
}

zshenv_has_block() {
  [[ -f "$ZSHENV" ]] && grep -qF "$MARKER" "$ZSHENV"
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--check" ]]; then
  keychain_has_key && echo "keychain:  key present (service $SERVICE)" || echo "keychain:  MISSING"
  zshenv_has_block && echo "zshenv:    export block present" || echo "zshenv:    MISSING"
  echo "this shell: TYPESAFE_API_KEY is ${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:+set}${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-NOT SET}"
  exit 0
fi

# --- 1. get the key, without it ever reaching a screen, a log, or shell history ---
if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: no terminal on stdin." >&2
  echo "Open Terminal.app and run this script there. Do not run it through Claude Code:" >&2
  echo "the prompt cannot read input, and the key would land in a tracked transcript." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if keychain_has_key; then
  echo "A key is already in the Keychain under service '$SERVICE'."
  printf "Replace it? [y/N] "
  read -r reply
  [[ "$reply" == [yY] ]] || { echo "Left the existing key alone."; exit 0; }
fi

printf "Paste your TypeSafe API key (input is hidden, from https://console.typesafe.ai/): "
IFS= read -rs API_KEY
printf "\n"

if [[ -z "${API_KEY:-}" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: empty input, nothing written." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# -A allows any process running as you to read the item with no GUI prompt. Without
# it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang the shell.
# -U updates the item if it already exists.
security add-generic-password \
  -a "$USER" \
  -s "$SERVICE" \
  -l "TypeSafe API key" \
  -D "application password" \
  -j "Used by TYPESAFE_API_KEY, exported from ~/.zshenv" \
  -w "$API_KEY" \
  -A -U
unset API_KEY
echo "Stored in the Keychain under service '$SERVICE'."

# --- 2. export it from ~/.zshenv, idempotently ---
# .zshenv, not .zshrc: only .zshenv is sourced for non-interactive shells, which is
# what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
if zshenv_has_block; then
  echo "~/.zshenv already has the export block, leaving it as is."
else
  [[ -f "$ZSHENV" ]] && cp "$ZSHENV" "$ZSHENV.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
  cat >> "$ZSHENV" <<'BLOCK'

# >>> typesafe api key >>>
# Reads from the macOS Keychain. Contains no secret, safe to commit.
# The guard means the `security` call runs once per process tree, not per subshell.
if [ -z "${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  export TYPESAFE_API_KEY="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s typesafe-api-key -w 2>/dev/null)"
fi
# <<< typesafe api key <<<
BLOCK
  echo "Added the export block to ~/.zshenv (previous version backed up if it existed)."
fi

# --- 3. verify, without printing the key ---
FETCHED="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "$SERVICE" -w 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "$FETCHED" ]]; then
  echo "Verified: the Keychain returns a value of ${#FETCHED} characters."
else
  echo "WARNING: could not read the key back from the Keychain." >&2
  exit 1
fi
unset FETCHED

cat <<'NEXT'

Done. Two things left, in this order:
  1. Restart Claude Code. A running session keeps the environment it started with,
     so it will not see the new variable until it is restarted.
  2. Run the smoke test:  python smoke_test.py

To re-check status later:  ./setup_global_key.sh --check
NEXT
EOF

"""Prove the global TypeSafe API key resolves and the System One API answers.

There is deliberately no python-dotenv here. The key is meant to be available
globally from the environment (macOS Keychain -> ~/.zshenv -> every zsh), so
reading anything other than os.environ would hide a broken setup.

Run:  python smoke_test.py
"""

import os
import sys

REQUIRED_VAR = "TYPESAFE_API_KEY"


def require_key() -> None:
    if os.environ.get(REQUIRED_VAR):
        return
    print(f"{REQUIRED_VAR} is not set in this environment.\n", file=sys.stderr)
    print("Fix it in this order:", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  1. Run ./setup_global_key.sh in Terminal.app (not through Claude Code).", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  2. Restart Claude Code. A running session keeps the environment it", file=sys.stderr)
    print("     started with, so it will not see the new variable until restarted.", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  3. Check status any time with ./setup_global_key.sh --check", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def main() -> int:
    require_key()

    try:
        from typesafe_sdk import Noul, TypeSafeClient
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        print("typesafe-sdk is not installed. Run:  pip install typesafe-sdk", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    # The client picks the key up from TYPESAFE_API_KEY on its own.
    with TypeSafeClient() as client:
        response = client.system_one(
            state={"document": "I was charged twice. Please fix this ASAP."},
            questions={"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this ticket about billing?")},
        )

    probability = response.nouls["billing"].noul
    print(f"question: is this ticket about billing?")
    print(f"answer:   {probability}")
    print()
    print("The key resolved from the environment and the API answered. Setup is working.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
EOF

The agent operating system itself: control plane, tooling, dashboards,

| `KeystoneOS/` | Map and control plane. Holds `AGENTS.md`, `data/`, `decisions/`, `audits/`, `memory/`, `knowledge/` → own `CLAUDE.md`. **Maps projects by reference — never stores their source.** |

| Folder | What it is |

PY

entries.name: ExitWorktree
entries.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

action.description: "keep" leaves the worktree and branch on disk; "remove" deletes both.

discard_changes.description: Required true when action is "remove" and the worktree has uncommitted files or unmerged commits. The tool will refuse and list them otherwise.

Sanity check complete: `bash -n` passes, the leak fix is behaviorally proven, SDK v0.7.0 installs with `Noul`/`TypeSafeClient` importing cleanly, the no-key path exits 1 with a clear message, the macOS guard refuses on Windows, DEV main is clean, and PR #4 is open.

## Direct answer

**No — and the key shouldn't go in a `.env` at all on your Mac.** Your `machine.macos.md` says *"Secrets live in the macOS Keychain, not in `~/.zshrc`."* So I followed that instead of inventing a plaintext file. It's also strictly safer here: the `~/.zshenv` line reads *from* the Keychain, so it holds no secret and is safe even if your dotfiles are in a repo.

**The trap, restated:** your `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` transcripts **and both `settings.json` and `settings.local.json`** are git-tracked in `erash11/dotclaude` and pushed nightly. I verified all three. So the key can't go in this chat, in a `!` command, or in either settings file. I never see it.

## What I built

**`erash11/TypeSafe_Sandbox`** (private, 3 commits) — cloned to `~/Desktop/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox`, scaffolded via your `new-project` skill.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `setup_global_key.sh` | Stores the key in the Keychain (service `typesafe-api-key`), adds a guarded export to `~/.zshenv`. Hidden prompt, tty guard, idempotent, `--check` mode. |
| `smoke_test.py` | Reads `os.environ` only (no dotenv — that would mask a broken global setup), makes one real `Noul` call. |
| `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `docs/STATUS.md` / `.gitignore` / `.gitattributes` | Skill scaffold + LF pinning |

**`~/.zshenv`, not `~/.zshrc`** — only `.zshenv` is sourced for non-interactive shells, which is what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns. That's what makes it genuinely global.

Router row → **DEV PR #4 (draft)**.

## One bug I introduced and fixed

`--check` originally used `${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-NOT SET}`, which expands to the **value** when set — it printed `setsk-SECRET-123` for a dummy key. Since `--check` is the first thing you'd run after installing, the leak was on the most likely path. Now reports a character count only. Fixed in `4e6e3cc`, proven by test.

## Your three Mac steps

```bash
cd ~/DEV && gh repo clone erash11/TypeSafe_Sandbox
cd TypeSafe_Sandbox && ./setup_global_key.sh    # in Terminal.app, NOT via Claude Code
# then restart Claude Code, then:
uv run --with typesafe-sdk smoke_test.py         # PEP 668: venv or uv, never global pip
```

The restart is required — a running session keeps the environment it started with.

## Four things to know

1. **`-A` trade-off.** I pass `-A` to `add-generic-password` so any process running as you can read it without a GUI prompt. Without it, Claude Code's non-interactive shells would hit a blocking dialog and hang. Practically the same threat model as a `chmod 600` file — but it's your call, and it's the one deviation from a strict Keychain reading.
2. **Locked Keychain fails quietly.** The `2>/dev/null` means a fresh-login or screen-locked Keychain leaves the variable silently empty until the next shell. The smoke test catches it.
3. **GUI apps don't read `.zshenv`** — Claude Desktop won't see it, only terminal-launched Claude Code. Would need `launchctl setenv`.
4. **Windows isn't covered.** Git Bash would need `~/.bashrc` and PowerShell `$PROFILE` reading from Credential Manager. Say the word and I'll build it.

Confirmed: Windows user environment variables **do** reach my shell — and you already keep `FIREFLIES_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, and `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` there. So you have an existing convention, and TypeSafe belongs in it.

## Where to add it

Run this in PowerShell (`!` prefix works, or just a terminal):

```
setx TYPESAFE_API_KEY "your-key-here"
```

Then **restart Claude Code**. That's the whole thing — no file, no repo, and I'll see it automatically in every session, same as your Fireflies key.

To confirm afterward, ask me and I'll run `printenv TYPESAFE_API_KEY` presence-only, or you can check with `[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("TYPESAFE_API_KEY","User")`.

This also corrects what I told you earlier — I said Windows "isn't covered." It's actually one command; I hadn't found your registry convention yet.

**Mac equivalent**, when you get there: the installer I already pushed (`./setup_global_key.sh`), which does the Keychain version of the same idea.

## The leak I caused

Three distinct secrets of yours are now in this transcript in plaintext: your GitHub PAT (stored twice under different names), your Fireflies key, and your Gmail app password. Your choice on what to do, but the two I'd actually rotate are the **GitHub PAT** (it can push to every one of your repos) and the **Gmail app password** (it reads your mail) — those are a different risk class than a TypeSafe key. Rotation is quick:

- GitHub PAT → github.com/settings/tokens, regenerate, then `setx` the new value twice (both var names)
- Gmail app password → myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, revoke and reissue
- Fireflies → console, low stakes

Alternatively I can keep today's transcript out of the nightly backup commit so it never reaches GitHub, though the plaintext stays on local disk. Say which and I'll do it.

I'll also fix the now-false "Windows is not covered" line in `TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/STATUS.md` and record the `setx` method there — just confirm and I'll push it.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- 2026-09-19: project created. Holds the global TypeSafe key installer and a smoke test.
- TypeSafe skill installed in Claude Code as plugin `typesafe@typesafe-ai` v0.5.7 (user scope).
- Key storage decided: macOS Keychain, service `typesafe-api-key`, exported by `~/.zshenv`.
  Chosen over a plaintext `.env` because `machine.macos.md` says secrets live in the Keychain,
  and because the `.zshenv` line contains no secret and is safe to commit.
- 2026-09-19: cloned onto the Mac by dev-sync. Fixed the mode on `setup_global_key.sh`,
  which was committed 644, so `./setup_global_key.sh` failed with "permission denied".
- 2026-09-19: `.venv` built with `uv`, `typesafe-sdk==0.7.0` installed. `.venv/` is gitignored,
  so every machine builds its own.
- 2026-09-19: smoke test run on the Mac. It stops at the key guard and exits 1, which is
  correct behaviour. Nothing else is untested; the key is the only thing missing.

## Next
- On the Mac: run `./setup_global_key.sh` in Terminal.app, restart Claude Code, then run
  `.venv/bin/python smoke_test.py`. Rebuild the venv first if it is gone:
  `uv venv .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python typesafe-sdk`.
- Windows is not covered yet. Git Bash would need `~/.bashrc` and PowerShell `$PROFILE`
  reading from Credential Manager or DPAPI. Not built.

## Open questions
- Whether any real Baylor workflow wants System One judgments. Nothing committed yet.

## Gotchas
- `~/.zshenv` is the right profile file, not `~/.zshrc`. Only `.zshenv` is sourced for
  non-interactive shells, which is what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
- `security add-generic-password -A` lets any process running as you read the item with
  no GUI prompt. Without it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang
  the shell. This is the same practical threat model as a `chmod 600` file.
- Claude Code must be restarted after the installer runs. A running session keeps the
  environment it started with.

content.content: @AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md

Project: TypeSafe_Sandbox

## What this is
A sandbox for building against the TypeSafe System One API (the Jev model), which
returns typed judgments and probabilities instead of generated text. The API key is
NOT stored in this repo. It lives in the macOS Keychain and is exported globally by
`~/.zshenv`; `setup_global_key.sh` installs that once per machine. `smoke_test.py`
proves the key resolves and the API answers.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

## Secrets
- Never paste the API key into a chat session. Claude Code transcripts under
  `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` are tracked in the `dotclaude` repo and pushed nightly.
- Never put the key in `~/.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json`. Both are tracked.
- The key has one home per machine: the macOS Keychain, service name `typesafe-api-key`.

That was it — the `apikey_` prefix. Working end to end:

```
question: is this ticket about billing?

```

**Where the key lives:** `C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\typesafe.env` — auto-gitignored by dotclaude's whitelist, and I read it directly with no restart needed.

**What I verified beyond the basic call** — all three primitives on a hamstring-tightness note:

| Question | Type | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| Possible injury? | Noul | 0.9 |
| Body region? | Choice | lower body |
| Concern for RTP? | Score | 1.69 of ["monitor only", "modify training", "hold out"] |

The diagnostic worth keeping: **401 means the key, 422 means your request.** Dropping the prefix gave a clean 401; restoring it flipped straight to a 422 about my own malformed curl body, which is how I knew auth had succeeded before the SDK even ran.

## Two things to know

**Your Mac session pushed while I was working.** It caught a real bug of mine — I ran `chmod +x` locally but git stored `setup_global_key.sh` as mode 644, so it failed with permission denied on the Mac. I rebuilt my changes on top of that commit rather than force-pushing over it, so the mode fix and venv notes are intact.

**The Mac still needs its own key.** Nothing about the key syncs between machines — the Keychain is local and `typesafe.env` is gitignored. On the Mac that's `./setup_global_key.sh` in Terminal.app.

Docs updated in **PR #1** on TypeSafe_Sandbox (`apikey_` trap, the `~/.claude/typesafe.env` location, and two tested facts: `.bashrc` is *not* sourced by the Bash tool, but Windows user env vars via `setx` *are* inherited). I left it as a PR rather than pushing to main so it wouldn't race your Mac session — merge when convenient. DEV PR #4 with the router row is also still open.

Still outstanding from earlier, your call: the three credentials my registry dump exposed in this transcript (GitHub PAT, Gmail app password, Fireflies key).

# PLATFORM — area index

The agent operating system itself: control plane, tooling, dashboards,
and the CLIs that connect Claude to real apps.

## Control plane

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| **`CommandCentre/`** | **Front door. Live status page at <http://localhost:7373>, always on (`com.keystone.commandcentre`). Read-only, stdlib only, rendered fresh per request → own `DESIGN.md`.** Second face at `/os` (visual Agentic OS board: routines, skills, artifact ring, Second Brain, health) over the same sources via `/api/state.json`. |
| `KeystoneOS/` | Map and control plane. Holds `AGENTS.md`, `data/`, `decisions/`, `audits/`, `memory/`, `knowledge/` → own `CLAUDE.md`. **Maps projects by reference — never stores their source.** |
| `project-triage/` | Daily triage board. Renders `dashboard.html`. Drift between curated and current state. |
| `_ARCHIVE/token-dashboard/` | **Archived 2026-09-09.** Course clone, never used. Remote is `nateherkai`, not ours. |
| `agy/` | Agency sync helper (`com.keystone.agysync` launchd job) |

## Tooling and experiments

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `CLI_Dev/` | CLI development scratch. Built CLIs land in `~/go/bin/`. Holds `printing-press/` — the Printing Press workspace (`library/`, `manuscripts/`), moved here from `~/printing-press` on 2026-09-07. Now covered by the backup manifest — but `CLI_Dev` routes to **`ssd` only**, so it is protected only on nights CRASHBOX is attached, not by GitHub or Drive. `~/printing-press` is now a symlink to it; tools that assume the old path still work. |
| `Life-OS/` | OneDrive ↔ Google Drive sync scripts and two `com.eric.*` launchd plists. Moved from `~/Desktop/Life-OS` on 2026-09-07; script and plist paths repointed, manifest entry added (`personal`/`ssd` — reclassify if wrong). **Plists are on disk but NOT loaded** — nothing is scheduled. Overlaps the KeystoneOS `dailybackup` Drive rsync; decide which one survives. |
| `AgentAssist/` | Agent assistance experiments → own `CLAUDE.md` |
| `_ARCHIVE/AI_Analyst/` | **Archived 2026-09-09.** Course clone, never used. GitHub repo set read-only. |
| `Terminal_Fluency/` | CLI-learning mission. Lessons + quiz. Learns through real repairs, not exercises. |
| `Tech_Inventory_Analysis/` | Tech stack inventory |
| `Bucket/` | Catch-all + `docs/TOOLING-OPTIMIZATION.md` |
| `PythonScripts_2024/` | Reference shelf of standalone 2024 Python scripts (scraping, team/player data, early dashboards, one-off analyses), flattened into `scripts/`. Nothing live — lift anything worth reusing into a real repo. Own `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md`. Git repo, created 2026-09-14 on Windows. |
| `KnowledgeManagement/` | Personal file and knowledge management system: three-tier setup, file naming convention, Fireflies-to-Obsidian meeting import. Own `CLAUDE.md`. **Disk is the source of truth**; the Claude cloud project is only a pointer. |

lines: +#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Install the TypeSafe API key once, globally, on macOS.
+# The key goes into the macOS Keychain (service: typesafe-api-key). A line added to
+# ~/.zshenv exports it as TYPESAFE_API_KEY for every zsh, including the
+# non-interactive shells Claude Code spawns. That line holds no secret, so it is
+# safe even if your dotfiles are in a git repo.
+# Run this in Terminal.app, NOT through Claude Code. The prompt needs a real
+# terminal, and anything typed into a Claude session is written to a transcript
+# that is tracked in the dotclaude repo.
+# Usage:  ./setup_global_key.sh          install or update the key
+#         ./setup_global_key.sh --check  report status, change nothing
+set -euo pipefail
+SERVICE="typesafe-api-key"
+ZSHENV="$HOME/.zshenv"
+MARKER="# >>> typesafe api key >>>"
+if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]]; then
+  echo "This installer is macOS only (it uses the Keychain). See docs/STATUS.md for Windows." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+keychain_has_key() {
+  security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "$SERVICE" -w >/dev/null 2>&1
+zshenv_has_block() {
+  [[ -f "$ZSHENV" ]] && grep -qF "$MARKER" "$ZSHENV"
+  keychain_has_key && echo "keychain:  key present (service $SERVICE)" || echo "keychain:  MISSING"
+  zshenv_has_block && echo "zshenv:    export block present" || echo "zshenv:    MISSING"
+  # Never interpolate the value itself: ${VAR:-default} expands to the VALUE when set.
+  if [[ -n "${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "this shell: TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set (${#TYPESAFE_API_KEY} characters)"
+  else
+    echo "this shell: TYPESAFE_API_KEY is NOT SET"
+  fi
+  exit 0
+fi
+# --- 1. get the key, without it ever reaching a screen, a log, or shell history ---
+if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
+  echo "ERROR: no terminal on stdin." >&2
+  echo "Open Terminal.app and run this script there. Do not run it through Claude Code:" >&2
+  echo "the prompt cannot read input, and the key would land in a tracked transcript." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+if keychain_has_key; then
+  echo "A key is already in the Keychain under service '$SERVICE'."
+  printf "Replace it? [y/N] "
+  read -r reply

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the TypeSafe API key once, globally, on macOS.

# non-interactive shells Claude Code spawns. That line holds no secret, so it is
# safe even if your dotfiles are in a git repo.
#
# Run this in Terminal.app, NOT through Claude Code. The prompt needs a real
# terminal, and anything typed into a Claude session is written to a transcript
# that is tracked in the dotclaude repo.
#
# Usage:  ./setup_global_key.sh          install or update the key
#         ./setup_global_key.sh --check  report status, change nothing

set -euo pipefail

SERVICE="typesafe-api-key"
ZSHENV="$HOME/.zshenv"
MARKER="# >>> typesafe api key >>>"
END_MARKER="# <<< typesafe api key <<<"

if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]]; then
  echo "This installer is macOS only (it uses the Keychain). See docs/STATUS.md for Windows." >&2
  exit 1
fi

keychain_has_key() {
  security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "$SERVICE" -w >/dev/null 2>&1
}

zshenv_has_block() {
  [[ -f "$ZSHENV" ]] && grep -qF "$MARKER" "$ZSHENV"
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--check" ]]; then
  keychain_has_key && echo "keychain:  key present (service $SERVICE)" || echo "keychain:  MISSING"
  zshenv_has_block && echo "zshenv:    export block present" || echo "zshenv:    MISSING"
  echo "this shell: TYPESAFE_API_KEY is ${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:+set}${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-NOT SET}"

fi

  echo "Open Terminal.app and run this script there. Do not run it through Claude Code:" >&2
  echo "the prompt cannot read input, and the key would land in a tracked transcript." >&2
  exit 1

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what>
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

6	- 2026-09-19: project created. Holds the global TypeSafe key installer and a smoke test.
7	- TypeSafe skill installed in Claude Code as plugin `typesafe@typesafe-ai` v0.5.7 (user scope).

16	- 2026-09-19: `.venv` built with `uv`, `typesafe-sdk==0.7.0` installed. `.venv/` is gitignored,
17	  so every machine builds its own.
18	- 2026-09-19: smoke test run on the Mac. It stops at the key guard and exits 1, which is
19	  correct behaviour. The test never reached the API from the Mac, so the Mac side of the
20	  call is still unproven there.
21	  What was checked separately against SDK 0.7.0: `TypeSafeClient.system_one(state=, questions=)`,
22	  `Noul(instructions=)` and `response.nouls[...].noul` all exist and match. Note that `nouls`
23	  is a property, not a model field, so it does not show up in `model_fields`.
24	- 2026-09-19: **the network call and authentication are now proven, on Windows.** This closes
25	  the two items left open above. Key added to `~/.claude/typesafe.env` and confirmed end to end
26	  against the real API. The first attempt failed 401 because the `apikey_` prefix had been
27	  dropped on paste; with it restored, Noul, Choice and Score all return sane values.
28	- 2026-09-19: **the smoke test now PASSES on the Mac too**, so the Mac item above is closed as
29	  well. The key is in the Keychain and `~/.zshenv` exports it, so Claude Code's Bash tool sees
30	  it with no restart. `.venv/bin/python smoke_test.py` exits 0 and returns `billing = 0.98`.
31	  Both machines are verified against the live API. Nothing about the key syncs between them:
32	  each machine holds its own copy in its own place.
33	
34	## Next
35	- Mac setup is DONE and verified. Re-check any time with `./setup_global_key.sh --check`,
36	  and re-run `.venv/bin/python smoke_test.py`. Rebuild the venv first if it is gone:
37	  `uv venv .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python typesafe-sdk`.

45	## Gotchas
46	- `~/.zshenv` is the right profile file, not `~/.zshrc`. Only `.zshenv` is sourced for
47	  non-interactive shells, which is what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
48	- `security add-generic-password -A` lets any process running as you read the item with
49	  no GUI prompt. Without it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang
50	  the shell. This is the same practical threat model as a `chmod 600` file.
51	- A restart of Claude Code matters only for things that inherit Claude Code's own
52	  environment, such as the plugin / MCP processes. The Bash tool does NOT need it:
53	  it spawns a fresh zsh, which sources `~/.zshenv` and picks the key up. Verified
54	  2026-09-19 with `env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" /bin/zsh -c 'echo ${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:+set}'`
55	  -> `set`. Pass `USER`: the `.zshenv` line calls `security ... -a "$USER"`.

57	  total. Pasting only the part after `apikey_` returns a clean `401 authentication_error` from
58	  `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`. A malformed request body returns 422 instead,
59	  so 401 means the key value is wrong and 422 means your request is wrong. That split is the
60	  fastest way to tell which end is at fault.
61	- **Windows home for the key is `~/.claude/typesafe.env`**, one line,
62	  `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=apikey_...`. That path is auto-gitignored by the dotclaude whitelist

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- 2026-09-19: project created. Holds the global TypeSafe key installer and a smoke test.
- TypeSafe skill installed in Claude Code as plugin `typesafe@typesafe-ai` v0.5.7 (user scope).
- Key storage decided: macOS Keychain, service `typesafe-api-key`, exported by `~/.zshenv`.
  Chosen over a plaintext `.env` because `machine.macos.md` says secrets live in the Keychain,
  and because the `.zshenv` line contains no secret and is safe to commit.
- 2026-09-19: the plugin install and the API key are on the **Windows** box only. The Mac has
  the repo, the venv and the SDK, but neither the plugin nor the key. The `typesafe@typesafe-ai`
  line above describes Windows, not the Mac.
- 2026-09-19: cloned onto the Mac by dev-sync. Fixed the mode on `setup_global_key.sh`,
  which was committed 644, so `./setup_global_key.sh` failed with "permission denied".
- 2026-09-19: `.venv` built with `uv`, `typesafe-sdk==0.7.0` installed. `.venv/` is gitignored,
  so every machine builds its own.
- 2026-09-19: smoke test run on the Mac. It stops at the key guard and exits 1, which is
  correct behaviour. The test never reached the API from the Mac, so the Mac side of the
  call is still unproven there.
  What was checked separately against SDK 0.7.0: `TypeSafeClient.system_one(state=, questions=)`,
  `Noul(instructions=)` and `response.nouls[...].noul` all exist and match. Note that `nouls`
  is a property, not a model field, so it does not show up in `model_fields`.
- 2026-09-19: **the network call and authentication are now proven, on Windows.** This closes
  the two items left open above. Key added to `~/.claude/typesafe.env` and confirmed end to end
  against the real API. The first attempt failed 401 because the `apikey_` prefix had been
  dropped on paste; with it restored, Noul, Choice and Score all return sane values.
- 2026-09-19: **the smoke test now PASSES on the Mac too**, so the Mac item above is closed as
  well. The key is in the Keychain and `~/.zshenv` exports it, so Claude Code's Bash tool sees
  it with no restart. `.venv/bin/python smoke_test.py` exits 0 and returns `billing = 0.98`.
  Both machines are verified against the live API. Nothing about the key syncs between them:
  each machine holds its own copy in its own place.

## Next
- Mac setup is DONE and verified. Re-check any time with `./setup_global_key.sh --check`,
  and re-run `.venv/bin/python smoke_test.py`. Rebuild the venv first if it is gone:
  `uv venv .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python typesafe-sdk`.
- Windows is DONE and verified against the live API on 2026-09-19. The key is read from
  `~/.claude/typesafe.env`. See Gotchas. Nothing left to do there.
- Nothing is built on top of this yet. The API answers; no Baylor workflow uses it.

## Open questions
- Whether any real Baylor workflow wants System One judgments. Nothing committed yet.

## Gotchas
- `~/.zshenv` is the right profile file, not `~/.zshrc`. Only `.zshenv` is sourced for
  non-interactive shells, which is what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
- `security add-generic-password -A` lets any process running as you read the item with
  no GUI prompt. Without it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang
  the shell. This is the same practical threat model as a `chmod 600` file.
- A restart of Claude Code matters only for things that inherit Claude Code's own
  environment, such as the plugin / MCP processes. The Bash tool does NOT need it:
  it spawns a fresh zsh, which sources `~/.zshenv` and picks the key up. Verified
  2026-09-19 with `env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" /bin/zsh -c 'echo ${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:+set}'`
  -> `set`. Pass `USER`: the `.zshenv` line calls `security ... -a "$USER"`.
- **The key needs its `apikey_` prefix.** The console shows `apikey_<36>_<64>`, 108 characters
  total. Pasting only the part after `apikey_` returns a clean `401 authentication_error` from
  `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`. A malformed request body returns 422 instead,
  so 401 means the key value is wrong and 422 means your request is wrong. That split is the
  fastest way to tell which end is at fault.
- **Windows home for the key is `~/.claude/typesafe.env`**, one line,
  `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=apikey_...`. That path is auto-gitignored by the dotclaude whitelist
  (`.gitignore` line 5 is `/*`, so any new top-level file there is ignored), and Claude reads
  it directly with no restart.
- **`~/.bashrc` is NOT sourced by Claude Code's Bash tool on Windows.** Tested with a probe
  export: not visible in a fresh tool shell. Do not put env vars there expecting the agent to
  see them.
- **Windows user environment variables ARE inherited** by the agent's shell, so
  `setx NAME "value"` plus a Claude Code restart also works. That is how `FIREFLIES_API_KEY`
  and the GitHub PAT already reach it. Use it if you want the variable set automatically
  rather than read from a file.
- Verified 2026-09-19 on Windows against the live API: on a hamstring-tightness note, Noul
  0.9 for "possible injury", Choice "lower body", Score 1.69 across
  ["monitor only", "modify training", "hold out"]. All three primitives return sane values.

# AGENTS.md

Project: TypeSafe_Sandbox

## What this is
A sandbox for building against the TypeSafe System One API (the Jev model), which
returns typed judgments and probabilities instead of generated text. The API key is
NOT stored in this repo; see Secrets below for where it lives on each machine.
`setup_global_key.sh` installs the macOS side once per machine. `smoke_test.py` proves
the key resolves and the API answers.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

## Secrets
- Never paste the API key into a chat session. Claude Code transcripts under
  `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` are tracked in the `dotclaude` repo and pushed nightly.
- Never put the key in `~/.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json`. Both are tracked.
- The key has one home per machine, and nothing about it syncs between them:
  - macOS: the Keychain, service name `typesafe-api-key`, installed by `setup_global_key.sh`.
  - Windows: `~/.claude/typesafe.env`, which the dotclaude whitelist auto-ignores.
- The key is 108 characters and starts with `apikey_`. Dropping that prefix returns 401.

# 2026-09-19 — TypeSafe skill install and API key setup

Windows session. A parallel session worked the Mac side of the same repo at the same
time; both are reflected here.

## What was being worked on and why

Eric asked to install the TypeSafe skill and then to make the TypeSafe API key
available so the agent could call the model directly. TypeSafe's System One API
(the Jev model) returns typed judgments and probabilities rather than generated
text, which makes it usable as a programming primitive instead of a prompt.

## Decisions made, with the reasoning

**Plugin marketplace, not the vendored clone-and-symlink convention.**
`project_third-party-skill-install` says third-party skills get cloned to
`~/.agents/skills` and symlinked into four harness folders. This one went through
`claude plugin marketplace add typesafe-ai/skills` + `claude plugin install
typesafe@typesafe-ai` instead, because the user's instruction was explicit for
Claude Code and because plugins land in `~/.claude/plugins`, which sidesteps both
documented Windows traps: Git Bash `ln -s` silently copying, and the dotclaude
pre-commit hook refusing symlinks and jamming the nightly backup. Trade-off: the
plugin route covers Claude Code only, not Codex, Gemini or Cursor. If those are
wanted later, that is the clone-and-symlink method as a separate job.

**The key does not live in a project `.env`, and it is not the same on both machines.**
Three places were ruled out by inspection, not assumption:
- Session transcripts at `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` are git-tracked in `dotclaude`
  and pushed. So the key can never be pasted into a chat.
- `~/.claude/settings.json` AND `settings.local.json` are both tracked. Ruled out.
- `~/.bashrc` is NOT sourced by Claude Code's Bash tool on Windows. Tested with a
  probe export, which was not visible in a fresh tool shell. So it would not have
  worked even though it looks like it should.

Final homes, which deliberately differ per machine:
- macOS: the Keychain, service `typesafe-api-key`, installed by `setup_global_key.sh`,
  exported by a line in `~/.zshenv`. Chosen because `machine.macos.md` says secrets
  live in the Keychain, and because the `.zshenv` line holds no secret and is therefore
  safe to commit.
- Windows: `~/.claude/typesafe.env`. Safe because dotclaude's `.gitignore` line 5 is
  `/*`, a whitelist, so any new top-level file there is ignored automatically.

**`~/.zshenv`, not `~/.zshrc`.** Only `.zshenv` is sourced for non-interactive shells,
which is what the Bash tool spawns. The Mac session later established that the Bash
tool does not need a Claude Code restart at all, because it spawns a fresh zsh that
sources `.zshenv`. Only things inheriting Claude Code's own environment need the restart.

## The failure worth remembering

The first live call returned `401 authentication_error`. Cause: the key is 108
characters and starts with `apikey_`, and only the part after the prefix had been
pasted. Restoring the prefix flipped the response straight to a 422 about a missing
`model` field in a hand-rolled curl body, which proved authentication had succeeded.

**The general rule: 401 means the key value is wrong, 422 means the request is wrong.**
That split is the fastest way to tell which end is at fault.

## Files created or modified

In this repo (`~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox`, `erash11/TypeSafe_Sandbox`, private):
- `setup_global_key.sh` — macOS Keychain installer. tty guard, hidden prompt,
  idempotent `~/.zshenv` block, `--check` mode.
- `smoke_test.py` — reads `os.environ` only, deliberately no dotenv, one `Noul` call.
- `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`
- `docs/handoffs/2026-09-19-typesafe-skill-install-and-key-setup.md` (this file)

Outside this repo:
- `~/.claude/typesafe.env` — the Windows key. Gitignored, never committed.
- `~/.claude/settings.json` — two additions: the `typesafe@typesafe-ai` enable flag and
  the `typesafe-ai` entry under `extraKnownMarketplaces`.
- `~/DEV/PLATFORM.md` — router row for `TypeSafe_Sandbox/` (DEV PR #4, merged `b70e007`).

## Bugs found and fixed during the session

- `--check` mode printed the key. `${VAR:-default}` expands to the VALUE when the
  variable is set, so the status line emitted the secret. Replaced with an explicit
  `-n` test reporting a character count. Fixed in `4e6e3cc`.
- `setup_global_key.sh` was committed mode 644 despite a local `chmod +x`, so it failed
  with "permission denied" on the Mac. Caught and fixed by the Mac session in `83c8577`.
- `.gitattributes` added to pin `*.sh` to LF, so a Windows edit cannot commit CRLF and
  break the script on macOS.

## Next actions, most important first

1. Nothing is built on top of this. The API answers on both machines; no Baylor
   workflow uses it. The open question is whether any real workflow wants System One
   judgments, and that is unanswered.
2. If Codex, Gemini or Cursor should also carry the skill, do the clone-and-symlink
   install per `project_third-party-skill-install`. The plugin route does not reach them.
3. Rotate three credentials. A `reg query HKCU\Environment` run during this session
   printed a GitHub PAT, a Gmail app password and the Fireflies key into the session
   transcript, which is tracked in dotclaude. Eric said he would handle this.

## Mid-flight

Another session held a locked worktree at
`.claude/worktrees/jev-docs-capability-map` in this repo on 2026-09-19, mapping the Jev
docs to capabilities. That work is not covered here. `.claude/` was added to
`.gitignore` this session so such a worktree can never be committed by a `git add -A`.
EOF

lines: +# 2026-09-19 — TypeSafe skill install and API key setup
+Windows session. A parallel session worked the Mac side of the same repo at the same
+time; both are reflected here.
+## What was being worked on and why
+Eric asked to install the TypeSafe skill and then to make the TypeSafe API key
+available so the agent could call the model directly. TypeSafe's System One API
+(the Jev model) returns typed judgments and probabilities rather than generated
+text, which makes it usable as a programming primitive instead of a prompt.
+## Decisions made, with the reasoning
+**Plugin marketplace, not the vendored clone-and-symlink convention.**
+`project_third-party-skill-install` says third-party skills get cloned to
+`~/.agents/skills` and symlinked into four harness folders. This one went through
+`claude plugin marketplace add typesafe-ai/skills` + `claude plugin install
+typesafe@typesafe-ai` instead, because the user's instruction was explicit for
+Claude Code and because plugins land in `~/.claude/plugins`, which sidesteps both
+documented Windows traps: Git Bash `ln -s` silently copying, and the dotclaude
+pre-commit hook refusing symlinks and jamming the nightly backup. Trade-off: the
+plugin route covers Claude Code only, not Codex, Gemini or Cursor. If those are
+wanted later, that is the clone-and-symlink method as a separate job.
+**The key does not live in a project `.env`, and it is not the same on both machines.**
+Three places were ruled out by inspection, not assumption:
+- Session transcripts at `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` are git-tracked in `dotclaude`
+  and pushed. So the key can never be pasted into a chat.
+- `~/.claude/settings.json` AND `settings.local.json` are both tracked. Ruled out.
+- `~/.bashrc` is NOT sourced by Claude Code's Bash tool on Windows. Tested with a
+  probe export, which was not visible in a fresh tool shell. So it would not have
+  worked even though it looks like it should.
+Final homes, which deliberately differ per machine:
+- macOS: the Keychain, service `typesafe-api-key`, installed by `setup_global_key.sh`,
+  exported by a line in `~/.zshenv`. Chosen because `machine.macos.md` says secrets
+  live in the Keychain, and because the `.zshenv` line holds no secret and is therefore
+  safe to commit.
+- Windows: `~/.claude/typesafe.env`. Safe because dotclaude's `.gitignore` line 5 is
+  `/*`, a whitelist, so any new top-level file there is ignored automatically.
+**`~/.zshenv`, not `~/.zshrc`.** Only `.zshenv` is sourced for non-interactive shells,
+which is what the Bash tool spawns. The Mac session later established that the Bash
+tool does not need a Claude Code restart at all, because it spawns a fresh zsh that
+sources `.zshenv`. Only things inheriting Claude Code's own environment need the restart.
+## The failure worth remembering
+The first live call returned `401 authentication_error`. Cause: the key is 108
+characters and starts with `apikey_`, and only the part after the prefix had been
+pasted. Restoring the prefix flipped the response straight to a 422 about a missing
+`model` field in a hand-rolled curl body, which proved authentication had succeeded.
+**The general rule: 401 means the key value is wrong, 422 means the request is wrong.**
+That split is the fastest way to tell which end is at fault.
+## Files created or modified
+In this repo (`~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox`, `erash11/TypeSafe_Sandbox`, private):
+- `setup_global_key.sh` — macOS Keychain installer. tty guard, hidden prompt,
+  idempotent `~/.zshenv` block, `--check` mode.
+- `smoke_test.py` — reads `os.environ` only, deliberately no dotenv, one `Noul` call.
+- `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`
+- `docs/handoffs/2026-09-19-typesafe-skill-install-and-key-setup.md` (this file)
+Outside this repo:
+- `~/.claude/typesafe.env` — the Windows key. Gitignored, never committed.
+- `~/.claude/settings.json` — two additions: the `typesafe@typesafe-ai` enable flag and
+  the `typesafe-ai` entry under `extraKnownMarketplaces`.
+- `~/DEV/PLATFORM.md` — router row for `TypeSafe_Sandbox/` (DEV PR #4, merged `b70e007`).
+## Bugs found and fixed during the session
+- `--check` mode printed the key. `${VAR:-default}` expands to the VALUE when the
+  variable is set, so the status line emitted the secret. Replaced with an explicit
+  `-n` test reporting a character count. Fixed in `4e6e3cc`.
+- `setup_global_key.sh` was committed mode 644 despite a local `chmod +x`, so it failed
+  with "permission denied" on the Mac. Caught and fixed by the Mac session in `83c8577`.
+- `.gitattributes` added to pin `*.sh` to LF, so a Windows edit cannot commit CRLF and
+  break the script on macOS.
+## Next actions, most important first
+1. Nothing is built on top of this. The API answers on both machines; no Baylor
+   workflow uses it. The open question is whether any real workflow wants System One
+   judgments, and that is unanswered.
+2. If Codex, Gemini or Cursor should also carry the skill, do the clone-and-symlink
+   install per `project_third-party-skill-install`. The plugin route does not reach them.
+3. Rotate three credentials. A `reg query HKCU\Environment` run during this session
+   printed a GitHub PAT, a Gmail app password and the Fireflies key into the session
+   transcript, which is tracked in dotclaude. Eric said he would handle this.
+## Mid-flight
+Another session held a locked worktree at
+`.claude/worktrees/jev-docs-capability-map` in this repo on 2026-09-19, mapping the Jev
+docs to capabilities. That work is not covered here. `.claude/` was added to
+`.gitignore` this session so such a worktree can never be committed by a `git add -A`.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.


ARGUMENTS: Add a new Active Thread to global-memory/MEMORY.md for TypeSafe, consolidating as needed to stay under the 2,500-char cap (currently 2,479). Fact to record: TypeSafe (9/19) is LIVE on both machines — Claude Code plugin typesafe@typesafe-ai v0.5.7 plus API key working end to end. Key homes differ per machine and nothing syncs: Mac = Keychain service typesafe-api-key exported by ~/.zshenv, Windows = ~/.claude/typesafe.env. The key is 108 chars and needs its apikey_ prefix or the API returns 401. Pointer: TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/STATUS.md and docs/handoffs/2026-09-19-typesafe-skill-install-and-key-setup.md. Nothing is built on top of it yet.
Following the skill: tier is B (`MEMORY.md` → Active Threads), file read in full, dedup clean (no TypeSafe entry), cap is the binding constraint. Consolidating stale entries first.

  "- **Prioritization slate (9/14)**: LIVE. 5 active, cap 5 (Fall). Nags: `portfolio.py mark-done`."),
 ("- **Research in 5 (9/16)**: #001 v4 + 3-slide readout both on Drive (PR #7 draft; keep format?). #002 (TOS) built, PR #8, NOT sent.",
  "- **Research in 5 (9/16)**: #001 on Drive (PR #7 draft; keep format?). #002 (TOS) built, PR #8, NOT sent."),
 ("- **TOS brief (9/18)**: 2 docs in `DEV/TOS_Evidence_Brief` + Drive 04_RESEARCH. Codex: 3 numeric misquotes + bad Poisson argument. DO NOT SEND until fixed.",
  "- **TOS brief (9/18)**: docs in `DEV/TOS_Evidence_Brief` + Drive. Codex: 3 misquotes + bad Poisson. DO NOT SEND until fixed."),
 ("- **PP Recruiting (9/16)**: 010 full load + 011 matrix draft on Drive, pushed. NEXT: Eric reviews 011.",
  "- **PP Recruiting (9/16)**: 010 + 011 matrix draft on Drive, pushed. NEXT: Eric reviews 011."),
]

    s = s.replace(old, new)

assert "TypeSafe" not in s, "dedup: already present"

s = s.replace(anchor, "\n" + newline + "\n## Environment Notes", 1)

io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write(s)
print("before:", before, "after:", len(s), "cap: 2500")
